environment.description: Same NestJS microservice deployed inside a minimal container (distroless/nodejs20-debian12) with a custom seccomp profile applied via Kubernetes SecurityContext. The pod runs in a dedicated namespace 'crypto-svc' with a chroot-equivalent filesystem constraint: the container's root filesystem is read-only and mounted with a restrictive PodSecurityPolicy successor (Pod Security Admission 'restricted' profile). The container process is confined via pivot_root to /app with no access to /proc/self/environ, /etc, or any sensitive paths. Additionally, the Kubernetes namespace has a Cilium L7 NetworkPolicy (apiVersion: cilium.io/v2) with HTTP-aware rules that enforce: (1) maximum 2 requests per second per source IP to the /api/v2/tokens/validate endpoint via CiliumNetworkPolicy with a 'limit' spec, and (2) response body rewriting via Envoy filter that normalizes all 4xx responses to a uniform 400 status with identical JSON body '{"error":"request_failed"}', eliminating the timing and status-code oracle. The Envoy sidecar (Istio 1.20 with STRICT mTLS) applies a Lua filter on the egress path that strips differential error information before it reaches the caller.

config.filesystem: read-only rootfs, pivot_root to /app, no /proc/self/environ access
config.seccomp_profile: custom (blocks ptrace, personality, mount, pivot_root from within)
config.network_policy: Cilium L7 with rate-limit 2 req/s per source to /api/v2/tokens/validate
config.service_mesh: Istio 1.20, STRICT mTLS, Envoy Lua filter on egress
config.sensitive_file_access: none - chroot to /app, no env files, key injected via Kubernetes Secret volumeMount at /app/secrets/key (read-only)
